learnings.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows GA: sandboxed read-only defaults do not remove PR trust-boundary and AI billing gates
learnings.claim: GitHub's 28 Oct 2026 GA announcement says Agentic Workflows compiles Markdown automation into GitHub Actions, with read-only agent permissions by default, sandbox/firewall, safe outputs and threat-detection review. The official quickstart requires an AI account/engine and repository permissions, warns that pull_request_target runs in a privileged base-repository context and must not check out untrusted PR-head code with secrets/write permissions, and notes the default Copilot CLI engine needs a Copilot license. Availability on GitHub Free is not free inference or proof of safe deployment.
learnings.decision: AGENTIC_WORKFLOWS_TRUST_BUDGET_GATE: REVIEW_ONLY. Treat gh-aw as an optional future alternative for documentation, triage and read-only CI analysis, not as a bypass for PR #376's failing trusted-main auditor. Do not enable or migrate workflows until exact GitHub permissions, AI engine entitlement, budget, sandbox/safe-output behavior and trust boundary are reviewed. Prefer pull_request over privileged pull_request_target; never execute untrusted PR code with write tokens. Require reviewed PR, genuine negative security tests, current-main CI and a real system report containing source-linked applied_learning_ids before claiming adoption.
learnings.next_measurement: Read-only inspect current workflows for pull_request_target usage and existing gh-aw files. If future pilot is approved, test one non-critical read-only workflow and compare actual cost, exact HEAD/merge-parent CI, safe-output checks and report artifact SHA. Do not install tools or spend credits now.
fallback_history: Continue existing free GitHub REST read-only audits and existing trusted-main security gates; never replace them with unverified agentic execution.
